question: Which genes change in the endometrial organoids when we add IL-1B on top of estradiol?
why: Bulk human organoid RNA-seq with a real treatment contrast in CEL.Treatment. The atlas's own rnaseq-vs-differentialabundance entry says "If you have no counts yet, both are needed in sequence", so naming both is following the payload, not hedging: acceptable_sets allows either answer.

question: Which genes are turned up or down in the mesenchymal MDA-MB-231 cells compared with the epithelial-like ones?
why: Bulk human cell-line RNA-seq, two subtypes in CEL.Type. Reworded after the first run: the original asked what differs "at the transcript level", which is standard wording for isoform-level analysis, and the model answered rnasplice 3/3. That reading was defensible, so the question was at fault, not the answer. It now names gene-level up/down explicitly.

question: How do the cell populations in these granulomas differ between the 4 week and 10 week animals?
why: Seq-Well single-cell macaque granulomas; NHP.Cohort carries the 4wk/10wk split.

question: What immune cell types show up in the lavage after IV BCG versus aerosol BCG?
why: Single-cell BAL, NHP.Cohort has the three BCG routes.

question: Which lung cell types respond to infection differently across the CC mouse strains?
why: CITE-seq mouse lung, MUS.Genotype = PWK / CC011 / CC024.

question: How many distinct cell states are in these granulomas, and does that track with bacterial burden?
why: Single-cell with TIS.CFU recorded. The correlation is downstream work; the pipeline is still scrnaseq.

question: What changes in the lung cells when the mice get the N297A antibody before Mtb infection?
why: Mouse lung CD45+ single-cell, MUS.Treatment1 = PBS / N297A / mIgG2a.

question: Run a splicing analysis on the samples isolated from these mice.
why: The lab ran expression (A.GEX), but these are bulk total-RNA mouse libraries with an Uninfected/infected contrast, so the same FASTQs answer a splicing question.

question: Are there any fusion transcripts in this breast cancer line?
why: Bulk paired-end human tumour-line RNA — exactly what fusion calling needs.

question: Can you get HLA types out of these macrophage RNA-seq samples?
why: Human primary macrophages, bulk RNA. hlatyping accepts RNA with seq_type=rna.

question: Can we call variants straight from the organoid RNA-seq rather than sequencing DNA?
why: Same bulk library rnaseq uses; the question is variants, not expression.

question: We already have the count matrix from the chip experiment — just run the group comparison for me.
why: A.GEX holds a counts CSV. The scientist explicitly does not want realignment.

question: Do the COL2A1-edited chondronoids use different isoforms from the wild type ones?
why: THE library-prep test. DNA.LibraryPrepProtocol says oligo(dT)-primed UMI-based 3' RNA-Seq: only the 3' end is sequenced, so isoform usage is not recoverable. Nothing in the sample-type fields says this — it is only in the prep text.

question: Run a splicing analysis on these granuloma single-cell samples.
why: 3'-biased single-cell libraries carry no isoform-level information. Pairs with lau-mouse-splicing: same question, different data, opposite correct answer.

question: What HLA alleles are these macaques carrying?
why: Macaques have Mamu MHC, not HLA, and these are 3' single-cell libraries. Two independent reasons to decline.

question: Can we call gene fusions in these mouse macrophages?
why: nf-core/rnafusion's callers and reference bundles are human. Mouse is not supported.

question: Can we look at miRNA levels in these macrophages?
why: smrnaseq needs a size-selected 18-30nt library. These are polyA/total RNA — the small RNAs were never captured.

question: Where are the ribosomes sitting on these transcripts?
why: Ribosome profiling needs footprint libraries. None exist here.

question: Which genes are differentially expressed between these samples?
why: Hi-C. Not RNA at all — the plainest refusal in the set.

question: Any expression changes in these duplex-capture samples?
why: Targeted duplex DNA capture. The question presumes RNA that was never sequenced.

question: I'd like to look at the transcriptome of these samples.
why: The cohort whose label and data disagree: A.GEX label, single-cell SequencingType. Underspecified question on contradictory metadata — naming both, or asking, is the honest answer.

question: Compare the infected and the uninfected animals for me.
why: Deliberately vague -- "compare the infected and the uninfected animals" names no measurement. On bulk mouse RNA both a gene-level and an isoform-level reading are legitimate, which is what the ambiguous class is for; the earlier singleton expectation contradicted its own class.

question: Do any of these produce a PCA and a sample-distance heatmap as part of the standard output, or would I have to make those myself?
why: rnaseq emits both from its DESeq2 QC step. That fact lives in the output guide and in no metadata field -- and it is the one the model missed when the docs were withheld earlier.

question: I need a filtered feature-barcode matrix I can load straight into Seurat. Which one gives me that?
why: Names a scrnaseq output artifact explicitly rather than the analysis.

question: I want a VCF at the end of this. Can I get one without sequencing DNA?
why: rnavar is the only atlas entry that emits variant calls. It is NOT one of the pipelines whose docs are fetched, so this is answerable from atlas prose alone -- a useful contrast with the cases that need the docs.

question: I need four-digit allele calls out of this, the A*02:01 kind of output.
why: Names hlatyping's deliverable in the form it actually appears. Human macrophages, so the species constraint is satisfied.

question: Give me a list of chimeric transcripts with their breakpoint coordinates.
why: rnafusion's output. Human tumour line, so the GRCh38-only constraint is satisfied.

question: I want per-event inclusion levels -- PSI values for exon skipping -- across these mice.
why: Names rnasplice's output rather than asking for 'a splicing analysis'. Bulk mouse libraries support it.

question: I already have the counts. I want normalised values and a differential table with p-values, nothing realigned.
why: differentialabundance's whole purpose, and the cohort's A.GEX record is a counts CSV. Also not a docs-fetched pipeline.

question: Can I get PSI values for exon skipping out of these chondronoids?
why: The output framing of sho-3prime-isoforms. A 3'DGE library sequences only the 3' end, so no PSI is recoverable however the request is phrased. Pairs with qout-psi-events: same deliverable, different library, opposite answer.
